title: Naomi’s Loss and Ruth’s Loyalty

questions.question: Why did Elimelech move his family to Moab?
questions.explanation: Ruth 1:1 (ESV): “In the days when the judges ruled there was a famine in the land, and a man of Bethlehem in Judah went to sojourn in the country of Moab...”

questions.question: What happened to Elimelech in Moab?
questions.explanation: Ruth 1:3 (ESV): “But Elimelech, the husband of Naomi, died, and she was left with her two sons.”

questions.question: Which daughter-in-law stayed with Naomi?
questions.explanation: Ruth 1:14–16 (ESV): “Orpah kissed her mother-in-law, but Ruth clung to her... Ruth said, ‘Do not urge me to leave you or to return from following you.’”

questions.question: What did Naomi call herself upon returning to Bethlehem?
questions.explanation: Ruth 1:20 (ESV): “She said to them, ‘Do not call me Naomi; call me Mara, for the Almighty has dealt very bitterly with me.’”

questions.question: What season was it when Naomi and Ruth arrived in Bethlehem?
questions.explanation: Ruth 1:22 (ESV): “So Naomi returned... They came to Bethlehem at the beginning of barley harvest.”

questions.question: Who were the two sons of Elimelech and Naomi?
questions.explanation: Ruth 1:2 (ESV): "...The name of the man was Elimelech... and the names of his two sons were Mahlon and Chilion..."

questions.question: How long did the family live in Moab?
questions.explanation: Ruth 1:4 (ESV): "...These took Moabite wives... They lived there about ten years."

questions.question: What did Naomi hear that prompted her return?
options: That the LORD had visited his people and given them food
questions.correctAnswer: That the LORD had visited his people and given them food
questions.explanation: Ruth 1:6 (ESV): "...for she had heard in the fields of Moab that the LORD had visited his people and given them food."

questions.question: Naomi urged her daughters-in-law to go back to whom?
questions.explanation: Ruth 1:8 (ESV): "But Naomi said to her two daughters-in-law, 'Go, return each of you to her mother's house.'"

questions.question: Why did Naomi say she could not provide husbands for them?
options: She was too old to have a husband and bear sons
questions.correctAnswer: She was too old to have a husband and bear sons
questions.explanation: Ruth 1:12 (ESV): "...For I am too old to have a husband. If I should say I have hope..."

questions.question: What town was Elimelech from?
questions.explanation: Ruth 1:1 (ESV): "...and a man of Bethlehem in Judah went to sojourn in the country of Moab..."

questions.question: Who was Elimelech's wife?
questions.explanation: Ruth 1:2 (ESV): "...the name of his wife Naomi..."

questions.question: What does "Mara" mean?
questions.explanation: Ruth 1:20 (ESV): "...call me Mara, for the Almighty has dealt very bitterly with me." (Footnote: Mara means Bitter).

questions.question: Why did Naomi say the hand of the Lord had gone out against her?
options: Because her husband and sons died
questions.correctAnswer: Because her husband and sons died
questions.explanation: Ruth 1:13 (ESV): "...it is exceedingly bitter to me for your sake that the hand of the LORD has gone out against me."

questions.question: What specific group of people were Mahlon and Chilion identified as?
questions.explanation: Ruth 1:2 (ESV): "...They were Ephrathites from Bethlehem in Judah."

key_verse_text: But Ruth said, “Do not urge me to leave you or to return from following you. For where you go I will go, and where you lodge I will lodge. Your people shall be my people, and your God my God.” (ESV)
